name: Ethyl hydroxyethyl cellulose
description: Ethyl hydroxyethyl cellulose (CAS 9004-58-4 ), also known by the trade name Etulos and approved as E230G , is a non-ionic cellulose ether used to control viscosity and flow behavior across water-based systems. It functions as a rheology modifier, humectant, and emulsion stabilizer in formulations where consistent texture and film formation are critical. In architectural and industrial coatings, it thickens water-borne paints. This material improves open time, reducing brush drag and sagging on vertical surfaces. Construction mortars and tile adhesives rely on it for water retention and workability, preventing premature drying during application. Personal care and cosmetic formulators use it to build viscosity in shampoos, lotions, and gels without compromising clarity or skin feel. It is highly effective in maintaining stability in complex mixtures. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it supports controlled-release tablet coatings and serves as a binder in solid dosage forms. It meets various regulatory requirements for safety and performance in medical applications. Ethyl hydroxyethyl cellulose is supplied as a free-flowing white to off-white powder. It is available in multiple viscosity grades to suit low- and high-shear processing requirements across different formulation types. Both technical and pharmaceutical-grade material can be sourced depending on end-use regulatory requirements.
